# pi-voicekit — Full Context for LLMs

> Entry point for AI assistants working with the pi-voicekit codebase.

This file used to inline architecture notes, a file reference, command tables and key
constants. That content was **removed** here: it had drifted — it described a superseded
design (one cloud recogniser, four modules, no TTS, no offline models) — and it duplicated
`README.md`, which is the maintained source. A stale second copy is worse than a link to the
real one, so this file carries only what is stable and points at the rest.

## Package identity

- **Name:** `pi-voicekit` (formerly `pi-listen-ng`; fork lineage `@codexstar/pi-listen`)
- **npm:** https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-voicekit
- **GitHub:** https://github.com/CyFeng16/pi-voicekit
- **License:** MIT
- **Type:** Pi coding agent extension (`pi-package`), TypeScript, Bun toolchain
- **Positioning:** local-only since 0.6.0 — every cloud backend removed from the code
- **STT:** 21 offline models, recognised in process by sherpa-onnx (batch, not streaming)
- **TTS:** 20 offline models (Kitten, Kokoro, Piper), synthesised in process
- **Punctuation:** in-process `punct-ct-transformer-zh-en`, marks-only, Chinese only
- **Languages:** Chinese, English and mixed Chinese–English (supported and validated); every other language in the catalogue is unvalidated

## Privacy in one paragraph

No audio is uploaded to a remote speech service. Capture, recognition, punctuation and synthesis
run inside the Pi process; playback writes a temp WAV (mode `0600`) and hands it to a local
player, then deletes it. One configuration the user sets up sends data off the machine, and the claim
above does not cover it: system audio routing (a player or capture tool that inherits `PULSE_SERVER` /
SSH audio is pointed at another host by the user). Text is not an exception to that claim: what the
user sends Pi, typed or dictated and then submitted, goes to whichever model Pi is configured with,
like every other prompt.
`tests/no-cloud-egress.test.ts` enforces the part that can be checked: no module imports the
removed WebSocket transport, names a retired vendor identifier or host, or calls `fetch` outside
`model-download.ts` and `tts-local-models.ts`. The remaining outbound step is model download,
once, from HuggingFace or GitHub releases. Upgrading from 0.5.x erases the
retired credential fields from `settings.json` on the first start and no longer reads an API
key from the environment; `SECURITY.md` names those fields exactly.

## Authoritative sources

- [README](https://github.com/CyFeng16/pi-voicekit/blob/main/README.md): current behaviour, setup, features, privacy section, full command table
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/CyFeng16/pi-voicekit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): release history
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/CyFeng16/pi-voicekit/blob/main/SECURITY.md): threat model, scope, design principles
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/CyFeng16/pi-voicekit/blob/main/AGENTS.md): repository rules for coding agents — language policy, gates, release policy
- [llms.txt](https://github.com/CyFeng16/pi-voicekit/blob/main/llms.txt): the short index for this repository

When this file disagrees with any of those, they win.

## Historical notes

- `docs/v6.0.0-tts-plan.md`, `docs/v7.0.0-tts-plan.md` and `docs/v7.1.0-ui-plan.md` are
  archived design documents. They describe the cloud TTS backend as it existed when they were
  written; 0.6.0 removed it. Read them for the reasoning, not for current behaviour.
